Text: The `javac` command compiles `.java` source files into {{c1::`.class`::extension}} bytecode files.
Extra: The resulting bytecode is platform-independent and executed by the JVM.

Text: Running `java` with the `-cp` flag specifies the {{c1::Classpath}} lookup path.
Extra: Using -cp or -classpath overrides the default search path of the current directory (.).

Text: In a JAR, the metadata manifest file must be placed at the exact path {{c1::`META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`}}.
Extra: This file dictates settings such as entry-points and class paths.

Text: An executable JAR requires the {{c1::`Main-Class`::attribute}} attribute to be defined in its manifest.
Extra: This allows running the JAR using the `java -jar` command without specifying the main class.

Text: On Linux or macOS, multiple paths in a classpath are separated by a {{c1::colon (`:`)}} character.
Extra: Using the Windows semicolon separator on Unix will break classpath resolution.

Text: On Windows, multiple paths in a classpath are separated by a {{c1::semicolon (`;`)}} character.
Extra: Using the Unix colon separator on Windows will break classpath resolution.

Text: If a class is found during compilation but missing during execution, the JVM throws {{c1::`NoClassDefFoundError`}}.
Extra: This is a LinkageError representing a discrepancy between compile-time and runtime classpaths.

Text: If a class is dynamically looked up by name at runtime but cannot be resolved, the JVM throws {{c1::`ClassNotFoundException`}}.
Extra: This is a checked exception thrown by methods like Class.forName() or ClassLoader.loadClass().

Text: The Maven declarative build system uses a configuration file named {{c1::`pom.xml`}}.
Extra: POM stands for Project Object Model.

Text: JUnit Jupiter unit tests are marked using the {{c1::`@Test`::annotation}} annotation.
JUnit's assertion method for equality is defined as `assertEquals({{c1::expected}}, {{c2::actual}})`.
Extra: Reversing these arguments will produce confusing assertion failure logs.

Text: Dependencies of your project's direct dependencies are resolved and fetched automatically as {{c1::transitive}} dependencies.
Extra: Maven and Gradle recursively fetch these dependencies from Maven Central.
